clause_i.reason: Take D to be the grouped held-key navigation mode across all seeds and attempts. In the L5 yaw range of plus or minus 0.030-0.060 radians, identical action history I_t can produce opposite visible lateral drift. A fixed q cannot choose the needed release or A/D correction for both signs and for the current doorway approach.

clause_ii.reason: The same D supplies a bounded-window policy g: the four chronological frames in the 400 ms window show the camera's lateral/depth trajectory relative to the projected bridge and narrow doorway, so g can select release-forward or the appropriate left/right correction for delivery at t+400 ms.

clause_iii.reason: Use H_t with forward held and the camera still inside the approach to the doorway, and let a be key-up-forward or the needed counter-steering transition. For 0 < tau < 400 ms, seven or more 50 ms ticks move the rigid camera body; at the high-yaw edge its lateral drift reaches the narrow door's nonpassing side. Success remains recoverable by a later back/strafe, but the same a delivered after the wall/void contact has strictly lower value because the non-clock collision state has consumed the safe opportunity.

configuration_reports.common_visible_process: The common witness is held-key camera motion: every 50 ms the rigid camera advances according to W/A/S/D and the generated yaw, while the canvas visibly shows the changing grid, bridge alignment, and doorway position. The 400 ms window predicts whether the delayed correction lands before the narrow doorway or after a rigid contact.

pre_run.reason: After preparation, a pre-run phase can keep only a fixed set of keys down. W (or W with both opposing strafe keys, which cancels) is the only constant forward route that can plausibly reach the exit; a single held strafe adds a large lateral component. Pure W reaches the doorway with lateral drift tan(abs(yaw)) times the approach distance. L5 permits only about 0.55 units of lateral clearance and the safe yaw bound is about 0.033781 radians, while generated abs(yaw) spans 0.030-0.060. The safe portion is therefore less than half, so the pre-run threshold does not override the mathematical Yes.

configuration_reports.label: yes
controls_available: Simplified interaction: click a projected crate or sign with the camera ray, use the visible nearer/farther depth buttons or wheel in 0.25-unit steps, aim the ray, and click RELEASE AGAINST FLOOR.
Navigation: W/A/S/D or arrow keys; the level uses a 0.38-unit movement step and a 50 ms movement tick.
Rewind Room resets the world, and Certify Impossible Move submits the replay after completion.
autonomous_processes: While no object is held and a navigation key is down, movementTick runs every 50 ms, changes the camera position using the current key vector and yaw, and applies void, wall, object, and doorway collision rules.
requestAnimationFrame continuously redraws the projected room, objects, reticle, and held-object preview; it changes presentation only and does not change the outcome state.
No autonomous placement, depth, or scale transition runs while an object is held; pick, depth changes, release, reset, and submit are input-driven.
grouped_control_modes: Keyboard navigation: key transitions maintain W/A/S/D or arrow-key state while 50 ms movement ticks advance the camera; this is the common real-time mode.

clause_i.reason: Take D to be the grouped held-key navigation mode across all seeds and attempts. In the L5 yaw range of plus or minus 0.030-0.060 radians, identical action history I_t can produce opposite visible lateral drift. A fixed q cannot choose the needed release or A/D correction for both signs and for the current doorway approach.

clause_ii.reason: The same D supplies a bounded-window policy g: the four chronological frames in the 400 ms window show the camera's lateral/depth trajectory relative to the projected bridge and narrow doorway, so g can select release-forward or the appropriate left/right correction for delivery at t+400 ms.

clause_iii.reason: Use H_t with forward held and the camera still inside the approach to the doorway, and let a be key-up-forward or the needed counter-steering transition. For 0 < tau < 400 ms, seven or more 50 ms ticks move the rigid camera body; at the high-yaw edge its lateral drift reaches the narrow door's nonpassing side. Success remains recoverable by a later back/strafe, but the same a delivered after the wall/void contact has strictly lower value because the non-clock collision state has consumed the safe opportunity.

configuration_reports.common_visible_process: The common witness is held-key camera motion: every 50 ms the rigid camera advances according to W/A/S/D and the generated yaw, while the canvas visibly shows the changing grid, bridge alignment, and doorway position. The 400 ms window predicts whether the delayed correction lands before the narrow doorway or after a rigid contact.

pre_run.reason: After preparation, a pre-run phase can keep only a fixed set of keys down. W (or W with both opposing strafe keys, which cancels) is the only constant forward route that can plausibly reach the exit; a single held strafe adds a large lateral component. Pure W reaches the doorway with lateral drift tan(abs(yaw)) times the approach distance. L5 permits only about 0.55 units of lateral clearance and the safe yaw bound is about 0.033781 radians, while generated abs(yaw) spans 0.030-0.060. The safe portion is therefore less than half, so the pre-run threshold does not override the mathematical Yes.

source_evidence.claim: L5 uses five focal lengths, yaw magnitude 0.030-0.060, the longest gap, 0.54 maximum key-slot scale, 0.95 doorway half-gap, 0.40 avatar radius, 0.38 movement step, 0.25 depth step, and a 400 ms four-frame observation window.
